messages:
Ethan (Customer): hey, hitting 500s on rerank when my candidate list has some weird chars. started after we ingested user comments with emojis + some legacy null bytes.
Jasmine (Support): sorry about that — can you paste the request body you used and the error id if you have it?
Ethan (Customer): sure, sample payload below (sanitized token):

curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/rerank \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxx" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"query":"nearby coffee","candidates":["coffee\\u0000shop","cafe","pizza\\ud83c\\udf55"]}'

Ethan (Customer): response was HTTP 500 with body: {"error":"internal encoding error","id":"err_01H..."}
Jasmine (Support): thanks. passing to eng-oncall, and can you confirm whether those \\u0000 are literal 0x00 bytes or the Unicode escape?
Ethan (Customer): the data is coming from a CSV import, so actual 0x00 bytes end up in the candidate strings. sometimes we also see lone surrogate halves after poor UTF-16 -> UTF-8 conversions.
Alex (Eng Oncall): grabbed the error id, looking at logs — worker-17 threw UnicodeDecodeError on decode in rerank preprocessor. stack snippet: 

  File "/app/runtime/preprocess.py", line 82, in sanitize_candidates
    s.decode('utf-8')
UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x00 in position 14: invalid continuation byte

Alex (Eng Oncall): repro locally with the sample payload, got a crash in the same code path.
Marta (Eng Runtime): thanks for the details. I can reproduce with a candidate containing a raw 0x00 and an isolated high surrogate (0xD8xx). The JSON parser accepts it but downstream code assumes valid UTF-8 and fails when creating tokens / computing embeddings.
Jasmine (Support): is there a safe customer-facing workaround we can tell them now?
Marta (Eng Runtime): temporary workarounds: 1) strip null bytes on client side (replace 0x00) 2) ensure proper UTF-8 normalization/roundtrip before sending 3) base64-encode candidate texts and use our alternate endpoint — but base64 path needs opt-in. I'll write a small node/python snippet they can run.
Marta (Eng Runtime): repro snippet (python):

  import requests
  s = 'coffee\\x00shop'
  r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/rerank', json={ 'query':'x', 'candidates':[s] }, headers={ 'Authorization':'Bearer x' })
  print(r.status_code, r.text)

Priya (SRE): noticed an uptick in 500s from that customer tenant yesterday. are these requests being billed even though they fail?
Sam (Billing): looking at metering — currently 5xx are counted for metered token usage. we should decide whether to credit impacted customers / change billing for these failure cases.
Marta (Eng Runtime): immediate mitigation: we can add an input validation layer that rejects non-decodable payloads with a 400 + error code INVALID_ENCODING and a helpful message. that prevents the crash and gives a deterministic behavior. longer term: sanitize (replace 0x00 with \\uFFFD or remove lone surrogates) and add tests in the rerank path.
Alex (Eng Oncall): agree — patch to return 400 is low risk and can go out as a quick fix. I'll open a PR and do a canary deploy.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started for patch/validate-nonutf8 (sha: a1b2c3) :rocket:
Marta (Eng Runtime): created issue INF-987: validate-and-sanitize-rerank-inputs. acceptance criteria: 1) API returns 400 with code INVALID_ENCODING for non-utf8 inputs, 2) optional sanitizer that replaces/removes invalid bytes behind a feature flag, 3) unit+e2e tests including surrogate halves, null bytes, mixed latin1 payloads.
Jasmine (Support): ETA on hotfix?
Alex (Eng Oncall): I'll cut a hotfix for hosted within 24h to return 400. full sanitize + test rollout targeted for next patch release (48–72h).
Ethan (Customer): thanks, appreciate the workaround. can you also confirm we won't be charged for failed requests?
Sam (Billing): we'll credit failed requests originating from the impacted tenant for the window 2026-03-12 02:00 -> 2026-03-13 14:00 while we investigate. I'll follow up with an email.
Marta (Eng Runtime): also adding a small exporter metric for "invalid_encoding_rejects" so we can alert if volume spikes. Priya can wire an alert threshold.
Priya (SRE): noted — I'll add a pager policy if rate > 5/min for a tenant.
Jasmine (Support): I'll follow up with the customer with the workaround snippet + timeline for the fix and the billing credit.
Ethan (Customer): cool, thanks all. keep me posted.
Marta (Eng Runtime): once canary looks good, we'll flip the validate flag globally and publish release notes that recommend clients sanitize inputs.
Alex (Eng Oncall): marking as high priority. assigning to runtime squad for implementation + tests.
Jasmine (Support): closing loop with customer after deploy. :eyes:
